newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 10.969 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 10.969 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day treasury bill rate rose to 10.969 percent from the previous 10.777 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The yield on the 182-day treasury bill rose to 11.343 percent from 11.076 last week.
The 364-day bill rose to 11.683 percent from 11.511, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The 91-day bills attracted bids worth 3.87 billion pesos, the six-months had bids worth 6.415 billion and one-year had bids worth 9.705 billion.
The amounts accepted were 1.5 billion each for the 91-days and six-months while the Treasury accepted 2.0 billion for the one-year bills.
The high for the 91-day bills was at 11 percent while the low was 10.875.
The high for the six-months was 11.375 percent and the low was 11.325.
The high for the one-year bills was 11.80 percent and the low was 11.625.
National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said the rise in rates had been lower than expected.
The bureau had expected the yield on the 91-day bills to rise by 27 basis points, she said.
For the six-months and one-year bills, the bureau had expected rates to rise by 35 basis points each, she said.
